invariant: Every canonical owner occurrence has exactly one total, unique, non-null typed relation under every schema-valid union branch.
summary: The proposed typed views do not normatively specify or database-enforce totality, uniqueness, nullability, cardinality, or failed-join behavior.
evidence: The decision lists view columns but not exact paths, occurrence IDs, joins, cardinalities, nullability, or failure behavior.
The deferred validator proves the generic graph but does not validate the derived views, so an incomplete join can silently omit an owner occurrence.
impact: The amendment does not prove guarantees equivalent to exactly-one physical typed ownership.
requiredClosure: Specify and database-enforce every typed-view mapping or retain the approved physical typed-owner tables.
closureEvidence: The coordinator rejected the equivalence amendment and returned IA-001 to the approved physical typed-owner implementation; no typed views will be implemented.

invariant: Direct SQL cannot forge validator conformance and commit a state the approved physical typed schema would reject.
summary: The equivalence proof assumes validator-2 conformance that the database proposal boundary does not establish.
evidence: The proposal trigger verifies envelope identity and hashes but does not execute JSON Schema, semantic-reference, or cycle validation.
A direct SQL writer can stamp validator-2 on invalid canonical content and faithfully project it into the generic graph.
impact: The generic-plus-view legal state set is broader than the approved physical typed-table state set under the direct-SQL threat model.
requiredClosure: Add a non-forgeable database validation boundary, narrow the threat model with evidence, or retain physical typed tables.
closureEvidence: The coordinator rejected the equivalence amendment and retained physical typed tables, which preserve database-level defense in depth without changing the direct-SQL threat model.

invariant: The typed research surface is read-only and the generic datum table is not a query escape hatch for runtime or research roles.
summary: The view amendment omits an explicit grants, revocations, security behavior, and actual-role test contract.
evidence: Catalog non-updatability alone does not prevent base-table SELECT or mutation privileges.
The decision does not name migration-owner, application-role, or research-role grants and revocations.
impact: A permitted role could bypass the claimed typed-only query surface.
requiredClosure: Define and test explicit role privileges and view security behavior if the view amendment is pursued.
closureEvidence: The coordinator rejected the view amendment; no new view/query privilege surface will be introduced by IA-001 closure.
